svg.text: Project Civic — dual CAN interface: STM32F407G-DISC1 (MB997) + 2 × NXP TJA1051T + 24LC512 + OBD-II
Net labels with the same name are connected. Every pin not drawn is left unconnected (open), exactly as on the board.
* NXP Fig. 18: input capacitor size depends on the regulator; C2 47 nF per Fig. 18.
No bus termination on U1/U2: the car's bus is already terminated; this is a stub node (NXP Fig. 18 note **).
Body-bus tap point: NOT on the DLC per the available
Honda/LEMON pages — identify it before wiring U2's bus side.
WP = VSS: writes enabled. Pull-ups: on the MB997 already (R29/R33 4.7 kΩ to VDD) — add none.
CN5 USB OTG FS (micro-B): to head-unit / laptop USB host —
CN1 ST-LINK USB (mini-B): flashing / debug only
PD4 = CS43L22 reset (on-board), firmware holds it LOW: do not wire
All other P1/P2 pins: leave unconnected.
PE4: drives a 5 V-triggered relay that switches 12 V at the
ignition START contact (not the starter load). PE5/PE6: only
via protected 12 V input stages — not designed on this sheet.
Why open-drain TXD/S + 2.2 kΩ to +5 V: the TJA1051T has no VIO pin, so VIO = VCC = 5 V and TXD/S need
VIH ≥ 0.7·VIO = 3.5 V (NXP Table 7). 3.3 V push-pull cannot reach that. PD1/PD2/PD3/PB13 are 5 V-tolerant (FT,
DS8626) and the firmware drives them open-drain. RXD is a 5 V output into FT pins PD0/PB12 (no resistor needed).
S pull-up = transceiver Silent while the MCU is in reset or booting; firmware pulls S LOW only in bxCAN Normal mode.
Power budget: each TJA1051 draws up to 70 mA dominant (NXP Table 7) — feed U1/U2 from U3, never from the board's
5V pin (≤ 100 mA as an output, UM1472 §7.4). On the bench without 12 V, feed the +5V net from a 5 V supply.
Grounds: OBD pins 4 and 5, U3, U1, U2, U4 and MB997 GND are one ground net.
References: UM1472 rev 9 · MB997 schematic E-01 · DS8626 · RM0090 · NXP TJA1051 data sheet · Microchip DS20001754 · SAE J1962 / ISO 15765-4
